name: Gridmatic Inc.
headquarters: Cupertino, California, United States — the registered corporate headquarters (20450 Stevens Creek Blvd, Suite 100; a 12,096 sq ft lease at The Towers at Cupertino City Center running to 31 December 2027) — with the retail headquarters and every press-release dateline since August 2025 in Houston, Texas (1201 Fannin St, Suite 262, a flexible-office suite); the company's own site publishes no address
employees: Not published. LinkedIn '51-200'; the retail site names 17 retail staff; aggregator estimates run from 34 (February 2024) to 74 (June 2026); 12 open roles across Cupertino, San Francisco and Houston in August 2026

ownership.ticker: Private (founder-owned; no venture capital on record)

summary: **BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** Gridmatic is a founder-owned, self-described 'AI-first power company' that has turned an ERCOT day-ahead trading edge into three businesses — a battery optimiser that tolls and floors batteries from its own USD 50 million fund rather than only bidding them, a Texas-Ohio-Pennsylvania retail supplier selling to data centres and bitcoin miners through brokers, and a seven-market trading desk — and every scale claim it makes ('most profitable participant in ERCOT's wholesale market', 'top-performing battery asset in CAISO', '1000+ C&I customers', '300 MW / 1 GWh under management') is its own; the independent record consists of two ERCOT batteries under its QSE, one CAISO battery it optimises, one SEC-filed ten-year revenue-floor offtake, and a job posting that says the company is preparing 'upcoming debt and equity raises'. **BACKGROUND.** Founded 2017 by Matt Wytock (ex-Google, Carnegie Mellon PhD); the California corporation Gridmatic Inc. dates from March 2016. Trading since 2019; FERC market-based-rate authority since July 2022; Texas retail electric provider certificate 10307 since March 2022; ERCOT battery operations since 2023 and CAISO since 2024; PJM retail since October 2025. Structure per filings: Gridmatic Inc. manages two Delaware limited partnerships and at least ten plant-genus-named Delaware LLCs — Rosa (Texas REP), Panicum (PJM retail), Equisetum (ERCOT QSE), Cupressus (CAISO scheduling coordinator), Isotria (ISO-NE), and four with new FERC authority in 2026. Named assets: Energy Vault's Cross Trails (57 MW/114 MWh, ten-year 'physically settled revenue floor', COD May 2025), Alpha Omega Power's Caballero (100 MW/400 MWh, CAISO, optimiser since COD) and Endurance Park (52 MW, ERCOT West). No revenue, profit or customer count is disclosed by anyone but the company.
ecosystemRole: The second pure-play merchant optimiser this corpus's software-and-optimization segment lacked, and a different animal from the first. Habitat Energy sells a desk on revenue share to owners; Gridmatic puts its own fund's capital behind the battery — a tolling or revenue-floor offtake in which it takes the merchant risk and the QSE seat — and then uses the same forecasts to run a retail book that sells matched power and day-ahead bidding to flexible loads. That makes it at once an optimiser (competing with Tesla, Habitat, Fluence, Stem and Hunt for ERCOT and CAISO mandates), an offtaker (the counterparty Energy Vault reports to its shareholders, and the model Modo calls 'the first known battery in ERCOT operated under a revenue floor contract') and a load-serving entity for the data-centre and miner demand the rest of the corpus builds for. Its ranking rests entirely on its own reading of ERCOT's public settlement data; no third party has verified the 'most profitable' claim, and the one independent leaderboard that can be read places its two ERCOT batteries eleventh and forty-third of 308.

productsAndServices.name: Battery storage optimisation, tolling and revenue-floor offtake (ERCOT and CAISO)
productsAndServices.description: The company's own description: 'We use AI-driven forecasting and optimization to maximize the value of grid-scale battery storage across energy and ancillary service markets', and, to owners, 'We sign tolling agreements with grid-scale battery owners and perform market bidding and dispatch to optimize performance and revenues.' Services listed for owners: 'ISO scheduling coordination, market settlement, resource trading, and risk management' (CAISO report, June 2026) and, for Caballero, 'resource trading and risk management; ISO market settlement; and asset performance and market update reports'. The commercial models are 'a guaranteed revenue floor and shared revenue above the floor' and tolling, funded by the USD 50 million Energy Storage Fund closed in November 2023 and 'earmarked to oversee the management of up to 500 MW of battery capacity in the ERCOT and CAISO markets'. Named assets: Cross Trails (Energy Vault, 57 MW/114 MWh, Snyder, Texas — a ten-year 'physically settled revenue floor' offtake with 'upside participation', Gridmatic as QSE, COD 31 May 2025), Caballero (Alpha Omega Power and Fengate, 100 MW/400 MWh, Nipomo, California — optimiser from COD in 2025), Endurance Park (52 MW, ERCOT West, under Gridmatic Equisetum LLC's QSE; owner not stated by the company), and 'a 50MW / 100MWh battery storage system in Texas' operated through the fund since 2023. Scale claim: '300 MW / 1 GWh under management' (December 2024) and '300+ MW of storage assets under contract across ERCOT and CAISO' (Modo directory, April 2025). Operating footprint: ERCOT since 2023, CAISO since 2024, no batteries claimed in other markets.
highlights: Independent measurement (Amperical's leaderboard built from ERCOT's 60-day settlement disclosures, January–July 2026, 308 resources): Endurance Park ranked 11th at USD 3.49/kW-month and Cross Trails 43rd at USD 2–3/kW-month — the only two ERCOT batteries whose QSE is a Gridmatic entity

Company-relayed benchmark: 'Endurance Park and Cross Trails systems, optimized by Gridmatic, topped the leaderboard with 115% and 99% Real-Time TBx capture rates, as reported by Modo Energy' for August 2025 (company blog, December 2025; the Modo table itself is paywalled)

Company claims: 'ERCOT BESS revenue in the first half of 2024 was $113/kW/year annualized — a 61% revenue uplift versus the average ERCOT revenue of $70/kW/year' (December 2024); Caballero 'achieved a 141% TBx capture rate, and 1.7x the median-performing asset's TBx capture rate' since COD (company CAISO Storage Report, June 2026); '#1 ranked 2 hour battery in TB2 uplift in ERCOT in 2025'

Energy Vault's SEC filings call Cross Trails 'the first physically settled revenue floor contract to be signed for a BESS in ERCOT', place Gridmatic in the non-investment-grade 'fixed toll plus upside' offtaker bucket, and record USD 18 million of project debt and a USD 12 million-plus ITC sale against the contract at about a 15% levered IRR; no floor price or upside split is disclosed

Modo Energy's April 2025 directory entry (self-written) claims '#1 leader in ERCOT day-ahead real-time energy trading' and a '48% revenue uplift over the weighted average BESS revenue in ERCOT, as tracked by Modo Energy' for one 2024 battery
productsAndServices.positioning: The company names no competitor on its own channels. Modo's US directory lists it beside Ascend Analytics, Caerus, CES, Equilibrium, esVolta, Fluence, GridBeyond, Habitat Energy, Hunt Energy Network, Intelligent Generation, Stem, Tenaska, Tesla, Tierra Climate and Tyba. Its distinction in that list is capital: the fund lets it be the offtaker, so it competes with Equilibrium, Octopus and the utilities' tolls as much as with Autobidder or Habitat's desk. Its CAISO report argues the edge is bidding, not siting — 'the impact of trading strategy can rival that of siting decisions' (Miller, Modo podcast, April 2025).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct with owners and developers: multi-year tolling or revenue-floor offtake backed by the Storage Fund (Cross Trails), or optimisation and QSE services for a fee or share (Caballero). Contact route assets@gridmatic.com.
targetSegments: Owners of merchant batteries in ERCOT and CAISO seeking a revenue floor to finance the asset (Energy Vault)
Fund-owned batteries needing a scheduling coordinator and bidder (Alpha Omega Power/Fengate)
Developers pre-COD (the fund's stated 500 MW target)
productsAndServices.roadmap: None dated. The fund's 500 MW target was set in November 2023 against roughly 200–300 MW named by mid-2026; four new FERC market-based-rate entities (Mays, Nyssa, Isotria, Calliandra; March–May 2026) and an August 2026 capital-markets posting citing 'upcoming debt and equity raises' imply expansion vehicles whose purpose the company has not stated.

productsAndServices.name: Gridmatic Retail — commercial and industrial electricity supply with the AI Load Optimizer (Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania)
productsAndServices.category: Retail electricity supply and flexible-load services
productsAndServices.description: A licensed retail supplier — Gridmatic Rosa LLC in Texas (REP certificate 10307, granted 16 March 2022, Option 1 since February 2024) and Gridmatic Panicum LLC d/b/a Gridmatic Retail in Ohio (CRES 25-140646E, launched October 2025) and Pennsylvania (EGS A-2025-3056545, launched February 2026) — selling fixed, block-and-index and index contracts to C&I customers, with three add-ons: '24/7 Carbon-free Energy' matched hourly through time-based environmental attribute certificates, demand response, and the patent-pending 'Gridmatic AI Load Optimizer', which bids a customer's flexible load into ERCOT's day-ahead market and Emergency Response Service on the customer's behalf ('greater than 5%' cost reduction; 'revenue share models... can include options with no downside exposure'). The retail business 'strictly refrain[s] from selling energy directly to consumers' and sells through brokers via a 'Deal Desk'. Named customers: EdgeConneX (a Houston data centre supplied with hourly-matched power since 2023 — 86.2% carbon-free in 2023 per the joint white paper — renewed in 2025), Data Factory (bitcoin miner, first Load Optimizer adopter, August 2025), Cholla Inc.'s 7 MW flexible-compute lab (November 2025, 'Gridmatic assumes all downside risk'). Scale claims: '1000+ C&I customers in two years, with 60% month-over-month growth' (June 2026); 'thousands of customers across ERCOT and PJM' (company podcast, August 2026).
highlights: Segments named: 'Data Centers, Universities, State & Local Governments, Manufacturing, Retail, Hotels & Hospitality'; the site's solutions pages are Flexible Loads, Bitcoin Mining and Data Center, and the footer carries the Texas Blockchain Council logo

Partners: Vega Energy Advisors (broker, August 2025), Satoshi Energy (flexible-compute, November 2025), Synota (daily settlement for miners — '5–10% reductions in energy costs', November 2025), OBM (real-time settlement and automated load control replacing '45–60 days of collateral', March 2026)

Supply: a 15 MW share of Avangrid's 120 MW Barton Chapel wind farm (2023–24) and a 10 MW solar PPA with Sol Systems' Mars Solar (June 2025) — the only named generation behind the matched-power product
No customer count, load served or revenue has been published by a third party; ERCOT's monthly load-serving-entity reports keep the figures confidential
productsAndServices.positioning: Sold on forecasting: 'As proof of the power of our forecasting, our AI has made us the #1 trader in the ERCOT day ahead market.' The Load Optimizer competes with the demand-response aggregators and the miners' own curtailment desks; the matched-power product competes with the hyperscalers' 24/7 procurement programmes for smaller data-centre loads. Ohio was entered explicitly on the data-centre thesis — 'AEP Ohio projects demand could surge from 600 MW in 2024 to 5 GW by 2030'.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Brokers only ('strictly refrain from selling energy directly to consumers'); a Houston-based operations team with a Cupertino engineering team; VertexOne billing.
targetSegments: Data centres and edge colocation in ERCOT and PJM (EdgeConneX)
Bitcoin miners and flexible-compute loads in Texas (Data Factory, Cholla)
Mid-size C&I — universities, manufacturers, hospitality — through brokers
productsAndServices.roadmap: PJM expansion beyond Ohio and Pennsylvania is implied by the FERC filings but not announced; Gridmatic Isotria LLC has held an ISO-NE market-participant seat since 2021 with no New England retail launch.

productsAndServices.name: Energy trading and power marketing (all seven US ISOs)
productsAndServices.description: The original business: 'We build AI models to forecast energy prices and submit fully-automated bids into energy markets.' The company trades 'across all 7 U.S. ISOs' and states it is 'the most profitable ERCOT day-ahead trader since entering the market in 2019, according to public market disclosures' — a claim resting on ERCOT's 60-day disclosure of day-ahead awards, which the company reads and no third party has replicated. Its 2021 storage report said 'DART arbitrage is part of our core trading business already without control of battery storage resources'. Market-based-rate authority: Gridmatic Inc. (FERC ER22-2525, effective July 2022, with two refund reports suggesting sales before authorisation), Gridmatic Panicum LLC (December 2024), Gridmatic Mays, Nyssa and Isotria LLCs (March 2026) and Gridmatic Calliandra LLC (May 2026); CAISO convergence-bidding scheduling coordinator Gridmatic Cupressus LLC since July 2021.
highlights: Forecasting stack as described: 'We build our own weather models that are the core of our power and price forecast models'; 'deep learning models to forecast prices in all 7 U.S. deregulated energy markets across thousands of locations'; 'operates at the nodal level'
Retail day-ahead cycle published for customers: bids by 10 AM Central, ERCOT clearing at 2 PM, hourly execution the next day

The trading edge is the input to the other two lines — the retail product 'as proof of the power of our forecasting' and the battery floors 'will provide both Energy Vault and Gridmatic with the benefit of Gridmatic's AI-based forecasts' (Energy Vault release)
productsAndServices.positioning: A proprietary desk rather than a service; the company's rivals here are the merchant traders and QSE-marketers it does not name. 'Silicon Valley software innovation with deep energy industry expertise' is the retail site's framing.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Not sold; proprietary trading through Gridmatic Inc. and its FERC-authorised affiliates, with the two limited partnerships supplying trading and collateral capital.

productsAndServices.name: Managed funds — Gridmatic Energy Investment Fund LP and Gridmatic Storage Fund LP
productsAndServices.description: Gridmatic Inc. is investment manager and Gridmatic GP LLC general partner of two Delaware limited partnerships filed with the SEC as 'Pooled Investment Fund — Hedge Fund': the Energy Investment Fund (first sale 1 July 2021; USD 26.2 million sold to three investors at a USD 1 million minimum; 'The Investment Manager receives customary management fees') and the Storage Fund (first sale 27 December 2022; USD 24.95 million sold to one investor at the January 2023 filing; 'capital commitments to $50 million' by November 2023). The Storage Fund backs the tolling and floor contracts ('backed by Gridmatic's previously announced Energy Storage Fund' — Energy Vault) and the Energy Investment Fund is the parent of at least the PJM retail vehicle: Gridmatic Panicum LLC is 'a wholly owned, direct special purpose vehicle of Gridmatic Energy Investment Fund LP', of which Gridmatic Inc. is 'the general partner, majority investor, and investment manager' (Energy Choice Matters, December 2024). Investors are unnamed — 'a leading energy investor' funded the first storage tranche.
highlights: Fund capital is the only outside money on record; the two Form Ds are the only Gridmatic filings on EDGAR and neither has been amended
The structure explains 'profitable without venture capital': the operating company takes fees and a majority interest while LPs carry the trading and offtake collateral
Job postings (August 2026) reference 'existing investors', 'board packages' and 'upcoming debt and equity raises' — outside capital exists at some level the company does not describe
productsAndServices.positioning: An optimiser with its own balance sheet is unusual in this segment; the closest analogues are the owner-traders (Hunt Energy Network) and the utilities' tolling desks, not the software vendors.
targetSegments: Institutional and family-office investors seeking energy-trading and storage-offtake exposure
productsAndServices.roadmap: A further raise is signalled by the August 2026 capital-markets posting; no fund, size or timing is stated.

recentDevelopments.headline: 'The Gridmatic Podcast' launches with three episodes; the retail president says the business 'scaled to thousands of customers across ERCOT and PJM in just two years'
recentDevelopments.read: The company now markets itself as a retailer first; the customer count remains unaudited and unquantified beyond 'thousands'.

recentDevelopments.headline: A Capital Markets Associate posting says the hire will 'support upcoming debt and equity raises: build the transaction model, manage the data room' and 'own the company's collateral posting requirements across market operators and counterparties'
recentDevelopments.read: The first public sign that 'profitable without venture capital' is about to be qualified; collateral is the binding constraint on a trader-offtaker-retailer.

recentDevelopments.headline: Inaugural CAISO Storage Report: 30 batteries analysed with a 'proprietary shadow clearing engine'; Caballero, optimised by Gridmatic, 'is the top performer' at a 141% TBx capture rate; 'About Gridmatic' states '1000+ C&I customers in two years'
recentDevelopments.read: Self-published research that ranks the company's own asset first is marketing as much as analysis, but it is the only CAISO fleet-level benchmark in the public record.

recentDevelopments.headline: Gridmatic Calliandra LLC files for FERC market-based-rate authority (ER26-2439), the fifth new Gridmatic entity to do so since December 2024
recentDevelopments.read: Vehicles are being created faster than businesses are announced; the plant-genus names give no clue to purpose.

recentDevelopments.headline: Gridmatic Mays, Nyssa and Isotria LLCs receive FERC market-based-rate authority; the same day Gridmatic Rosa files its Texas Emergency Operations Plan from the Houston office, with Hung (Jackson) Vo signing as 'President of Gridmatic Inc.'
recentDevelopments.read: A retail executive attesting as the parent's president, from a coworking suite, while the corporate HQ remains a Cupertino lease — the company's centre of gravity has moved to Texas faster than its paperwork.

recentDevelopments.headline: OBM's daily settlement and automated load control combined with Gridmatic's forecasting for large flexible loads, replacing '45–60 days of collateral'
recentDevelopments.read: Collateral, not price, is the product for miners; daily settlement lets Gridmatic serve loads its own balance sheet could not otherwise carry.

recentDevelopments.headline: Gridmatic Retail launches in Pennsylvania (PJM); first appearance of the boilerplate 'the most profitable participant in ERCOT's wholesale market... Profitable without venture capital'; dateline Houston
recentDevelopments.read: The ownership claim and the profitability claim arrive together and are both unverifiable from outside; the dateline change from Cupertino (October 2025) to Houston is the visible fact.

recentDevelopments.headline: Company blog: 'Endurance Park and Cross Trails systems, optimized by Gridmatic, topped the leaderboard with 115% and 99% Real-Time TBx capture rates, as reported by Modo Energy' for August 2025
recentDevelopments.read: The first public naming of Endurance Park as a Gridmatic-optimised asset; the Modo table it cites is paywalled, so the figure is company-relayed.

recentDevelopments.headline: Cholla Inc. selects Gridmatic 'through competitive bidding' for its 7 MW flexible-compute lab in Mitchell County, Texas, with Satoshi Energy; 'Gridmatic assumes all downside risk, guaranteeing Cholla only upside savings'
recentDevelopments.read: The Load Optimizer sold as a no-lose proposition to the customer means Gridmatic's own book carries the forecast error.

recentDevelopments.headline: Gridmatic Retail launches in Ohio — 'first operations within PJM Interconnection' — citing AEP Ohio's data-centre forecast of 600 MW in 2024 to 5 GW by 2030; dateline Cupertino

relationships.note: The other pure-play merchant optimiser in this corpus; both are quantified in Modo Energy's April 2025 US directory, where Habitat claims 'over 1,300 MW' in ERCOT and Gridmatic '300+ MW' across ERCOT and CAISO.
relationships.context: The two compete for the same ERCOT owners but on different terms: Habitat sells a desk on revenue share and originates floors backed by insurers, Gridmatic tolls and floors batteries from its own fund and adds a retail book. Neither names the other on its own channels; Modo's tolling explainer lists Habitat's Octopus toll and Gridmatic's Cross Trails floor in the same table of ERCOT offtake deals.

relationships.note: Autobidder is the vendor-bundled alternative to a third-party optimiser in ERCOT and CAISO; Tesla and Gridmatic filed side by side in the PUCT's storage-scheduling project in October 2025.
relationships.context: Modo's US directory lists both. The PUCT's Project 58379 order names Gridmatic among commenters alongside Tesla, Hunt Energy Network and Jupiter Power. No commercial link is on record.

relationships.note: Fluence's dossier positions Mosaic against 'independent optimizers (Gridmatic, Habitat Energy et al.)'; both appear in Modo's US directory.
relationships.context: Fluence sells Mosaic bidding software to owners of any hardware; Gridmatic competes for those owners with a toll or floor rather than a licence. No commercial link between them is on record.

relationships.note: Both listed in Modo's April 2025 directory; the Stem dossier records that Modo quantifies Gridmatic's performance and describes Stem in capability-only language. Gridmatic's CMO was an early marketing hire at Stem.
relationships.context: Stem delivers QSE services through partners while Gridmatic holds its own QSE entity; they contest the same ERCOT and CAISO merchant fleets. Leesa Lee's bio cites 'successful IPOs at Enphase and Stem' — a career link, not a commercial one.

relationships.note: An owner-trader with its own QSE (TraDER) beside a fund-backed optimiser-offtaker; both commented in PUCT Project 58379 and both sit in Modo's US directory.

policyExposure.exposure: RTC+B replaced the day-ahead ancillary-service awards that Gridmatic's own reports showed supplying most ERCOT battery revenue (ancillary services 96.4% of the 2021 revenue stack; RRS 59% of 2022's) with five-minute co-optimised clearing and single-model battery settlement. The company's Equisetum QSE comments to the PUCT (October 2025) describe scheduling energy storage with 'a look-ahead horizon (e.g., ~24 hours) with explicit uncertainty' under the new design, and its December 2025 blog anticipates the 'RTC+B reforms'. Its two ERCOT batteries ranked 11th and 43rd of 308 on public settlements in the first seven months under the regime.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that Gridmatic's strategy is to monetise one forecasting engine three ways — proprietary trading, fund-backed battery offtake and a retail book for flexible load — and that the fund structure, not venture equity, is what has financed the last two. Basis: the company's own four-line description of what it does; both Form Ds naming Gridmatic Inc. as manager and majority investor; Energy Vault's statement that the Cross Trails floor is 'backed by Gridmatic's previously announced Energy Storage Fund'; and the retail SPV's ownership by the Energy Investment Fund per Energy Choice Matters.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that the company is independent and founder-controlled and that no change of control has occurred through 2026-09-12. Basis: no acquisition, stake or merger in SEC full-text search, the Federal Register, trade press or the registries; the CEO signing every filing; 'independently owned' on the retail site. Collection gap: the cap table and the LP investors are undisclosed, and August 2026 job postings reference 'upcoming debt and equity raises' — the independence claim should be re-read at the first refresh.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that 'HQ Houston' is true of the retail business and the press identity and false of the corporation, and that the distinction matters for the sale-side reader. Basis: GLEIF, LinkedIn, the PUCT record and both Form Ds give Cupertino as the corporate address; a CMBS rent roll shows a Cupertino lease to end-2027; the Houston address is a flexible-office suite and is described by the company itself as the 'retail headquarters'; engineering roles are posted in Cupertino and San Francisco, retail roles in Houston. The company's own site publishes no address at all.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the offtake business is smaller than its rhetoric: roughly 200 MW named against a 500 MW fund target set in 2023, and two ERCOT batteries whose public-settlement revenue ranks 11th and 43rd of 308. Basis: Amperical's leaderboard, the named-asset list, and the three different bases on which the company states 300 MW. Against this, the December 2025 blog's Modo-attributed capture rates of 115% and 99% for August 2025 point to strong bidding on those assets; capture rate and revenue rank measure different things and both can be true.

5. **(Low confidence)** We assess that the retail book, not storage, is where the company's growth and its risk now sit. Basis: '1000+ C&I customers' and '60% month-over-month growth' in June 2026, three states in twelve months, products in which 'Gridmatic assumes all downside risk', and an OBM partnership aimed at collateral relief; the capital-markets posting names 'collateral posting requirements across market operators and counterparties' as the hire's first responsibility. No customer, load or margin figure exists to test this.

**Collection gaps.** No financial statements; no LP names; the purpose of Gridmatic Iseia, Euphrasia, Mays, Nyssa and Calliandra LLCs; the owner of Endurance Park; Erin Kogan's status as CFO; the content of Modo's paywalled optimiser rankings; sec.gov was blocked and Form D texts were read through EDGAR full-text search and archived copies; businesswire.com returned 403 and releases were read from company and Yahoo copies.

**Indicators to watch.** *A Form D for Gridmatic Inc. or a named investor* — the equity raise the August 2026 posting anticipates would end 'without venture capital'. *A second SEC-filed offtake* — any listed owner naming Gridmatic as toller would show the fund model repeating beyond Energy Vault. *Amperical's and Modo's 2026 full-year ERCOT tables* — whether Endurance Park and Cross Trails hold top-quartile revenue through a full year of RTC+B. *A PJM battery or a New England retail launch* — what the Isotria, Mays, Nyssa and Calliandra vehicles are for. *GLEIF or PUCT address changes* — whether the corporation follows the datelines to Houston when the Cupertino lease ends in December 2027.
